_comment: Everything the quote document and the customer's message say about the business. Edit here, never in code — same convention as outputs/crm/offers.json and voice-scripts.json. Swapping this file is how the same system serves a different client.
name: FIXITT Glass & Aluminium
tagline: Glass and aluminium, 24 hours a day, 365 days a year
_vat_note: Left off until Zaheer confirms. Set vat_registered true and fill vat_number, and prices are then treated as VAT-inclusive. Never invent a VAT number.
promises: Two-year guarantee on spares and workmanship
We'll beat any written quote by 5%
Emergency callouts, 24 hours a day, 365 days a year
_trust_note: Taken verbatim from fixittglass.co.za on 2026-08-21 and shown as a quiet strip on the quote page. NOTE fixitt.co.za is a DIFFERENT company (appliance repair, 021 699 3153) -- never use it as a source for this business. Only claims the company makes about itself in public belong here; never invent one, and drop any line Zaheer will not stand behind.
trust: Preferred supplier to the University of Cape Town and the Radisson Waterfront
Approved by and affiliated to most insurance companies
_brand_note: The quote page's palette. Set from fixittglass.co.za once Heinrich sends a screenshot -- neither their site nor fixitt.co.za exposes a colour in its markup (both render through JS and placeholder SVGs), so these are a considered default, not their real brand. Changing them here re-skins the page with no code change. 'pay' is deliberately a different hue from 'accent' so the pay button never reads as just another link.
_banking_note: Shown on the quote page under the Pay button, for anyone who would rather do an EFT. THE PLACEHOLDERS BELOW ARE NOT REAL AND THE SECTION STAYS HIDDEN UNTIL THEY ARE REPLACED -- banking_details() returns nothing while any value still starts with 'FILL'. Never invent an account number. For a real install these must be the CLIENT's account, not Boschly's, or their customer's money arrives in the wrong bank.

banking.reference_label: Use your quote number as the reference

terms: This quote is valid for {validity_days} days from the date of issue. Prices assume access to the opening as inspected on site. Any additional work found on the day will be quoted separately and agreed with you before it is carried out.
_customer_message_note: The WhatsApp the customer receives — ONE short message carrying ONE link, changed 2026-08-21. It used to attach the PDF and paste a second Paystack URL underneath, which meant three things to look at and a document that a phone opens in a viewer she then has to back out of. Now the link is the whole thing: it opens a branded page with the quote, the banking details and a big Pay button. {first_name} {business} {quote_number} {total} {validity_days} {phone} are filled in; every figure is rendered by code so it always matches the page and the amount the link actually charges.

customer_message.link_line: Tap here to view it and pay securely:
customer_message.validity: The quote is valid for {validity_days} days.
customer_message.cta: Reply *YES* and we'll book the installation.

_customer_email_note: Sent alongside the WhatsApp when the technician gives an email address, with the same PDF attached.

customer_email.subject: Your quote from {business} — {quote_number}

_reply_note: What the customer gets back when they reply to the quote.

customer_reply_ack.accepted: That's great, thank you! We've got it — someone from {business} will call you shortly to book a date.
customer_reply_ack.other: Thanks {first_name}, we've got your message. Someone from {business} will come back to you shortly.

_technicians_note: Display names for the numbers that issue quotes — this is what prints under 'Quoted by'. Only list a number that really is a technician. It must be the same set as QUOTE_TECHNICIANS on Railway, and a listed number can never be treated as a customer, so a phone that is meant to RECEIVE quotes belongs in neither.
_payment_note: The payment link that travels with the quote. SET TO 100 on Heinrich's instruction 2026-08-21: the customer is asked for the full amount they agreed, not a deposit, and every 'deposit' word flips to 'payment' on its own. 50 asks for half up front; 0 turns the link off entirely, all without touching code. Nothing here decides anything on its own -- services/payments.py only builds a link for the amount it is handed. STILL A BUSINESS DECISION FOR ZAHEER when he goes live: emergency callouts are usually settled on completion, while fabricated work needs materials paid for up front.

payment._receipt_note: Paystack REQUIRES an email on every transaction and sends the receipt there. Most jobs are quoted with a name and a number only, so this is the fallback. It is Heinrich's address ON PURPOSE while this is a demo -- a test payment must never drop a receipt into a prospect's inbox. Change it to the client's own address the day they go live.
payment._label_note: {deposit} and {total} are filled by code; never write a figure here.
payment.quote_line: To get started, the deposit is *{deposit}* — you can pay it securely here:
payment.accept_line: Here's the secure link for the *{deposit}* deposit:
payment.paid_ack: Payment received, thank you! We'll be in touch shortly to book the date.
payment.pdf_line: A secure payment link for the {deposit} deposit was sent with this quote on WhatsApp.
payment.full_pdf_line: A secure payment link for {deposit} was sent with this quote on WhatsApp.
